_comment: THE GROUP KEY DERIVATION and THE SEALED ENVELOPE, pinned. A browser extension is a first-class node on the plane, so both halves must reproduce under WebCrypto.
_warning: `root_hex` is bytes(range(32)) — published test material. It is not a key and must never be one.

derivation._algorithm: HKDF-SHA256, salt=None (RFC 5869 default: a zero-filled string of hash length, i.e. 32 zero bytes), info=UTF-8 of 'comms:group:<group>', 32 bytes out.
derivation._webcrypto: crypto.subtle.importKey('raw', root, 'HKDF', false, ['deriveBits']) then deriveBits({name:'HKDF', hash:'SHA-256', salt:new Uint8Array(32), info:new TextEncoder().encode('comms:group:'+group)}, key, 256)

envelope._format: base64url(b'BSL1' + nonce(12) + AES-256-GCM ciphertext with 16-byte tag appended), AAD = the target artifact id as UTF-8.
envelope._replaces: Fernet (until 2026-08-04) — AES-128-CBC + HMAC-SHA256 in a bespoke container that no browser implements, which put the whole edge profile out of reach.
envelope._webcrypto: crypto.subtle.decrypt({name:'AES-GCM', iv:nonce, additionalData:aad, tagLength:128}, key, ciphertext)
envelope._note: The envelope is NOT pinned by a fixed string: the nonce is random per seal, so a pinned ciphertext would only pin the nonce. The derivation above is what a second implementation needs to match; the envelope is verified by decrypting these.
